llm.prompt_addendum_reasoning:
-------------------------------------------------------------------
P6 DYNAMIC-POOL PER-EPISODE ANALYSIS DIRECTIVE
-------------------------------------------------------------------
CONTEXT — what role this episode plays:
This failure was observed while the policy rolled out on the CURRENT
CORRECTION POOL. Note that this pool is GROWING: every round the
downstream cross-episode reasoner adds new layouts to it, and the
policy must learn to handle the entire growing pool. Your analysis,
combined with the other failures from this round, will inform which
NEW layouts get appended to the pool next.

Crucially: there is also a separate held-out evaluation set of 50
layouts that you will NEVER see and that no demo collector ever
touches. The held-out SR is the only published number. Do NOT
speculate about specific held-out configurations.

WHAT TO REASON ABOUT:
  * The FAILURE MODE this episode reveals — corridor side, fire-block
    pattern, visual feature missed, recovery the policy lacks.
  * Whether the TKF block (when present) flags this corridor / mode as
    NOT_FOUND, PARTIAL, or FOUND in the existing demo bank. The bank
    reflects everything the policy has been trained on so far. TKF
    gaps are exactly what dynamic-pool expansion targets.
  * Whether the RAG retrievals indicate this is recurring across rounds
    — recurrence is evidence that previous pool extensions did not
    cover this mode adequately.
  * Whether the KAG vocabulary contains a name that fits this episode;
    use that name verbatim in section 5.

WHAT NOT TO SPEND TOKENS ON:
  * Long step-by-step "how to walk through this maze" instructions.
    Section 5 still requests a corridor + path as a sanity anchor —
    keep it short. Movement-level planning is the prescription stage's
    job, not yours; your value is failure-mode identification grounded
    in TKF / KAG / RAG signals.
  * Held-out speculation. You do not see the held-out set.

Be specific to THIS episode but written so the cross-episode reasoner
can extract the failure-mode signature in one pass.
llm.prompt_addendum_cross_episode:
-------------------------------------------------------------------
P6 DYNAMIC-POOL CROSS-EPISODE PRESCRIPTION DIRECTIVE (v2)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
YOUR JOB IN ONE SENTENCE:
Output a list of NEW maze layouts that, taken together, would let
the policy generalise to a randomised held-out distribution you
cannot see. The held-out set is drawn uniformly from 5x5 / 3-fire /
Manhattan>=4 layouts. Covering it requires VARIETY, not minimum
cleverness.

WHAT YOU PRODUCE:
Concrete (start_pos, goal_pos, fire_positions) layouts that get
appended to the active correction pool. Demos are collected on them
via BFS and the policy is retrained.

=================================================================
HARD COUNT RULE — overrides any prior conservative guidance:
=================================================================
Total recommended_layouts across all clusters MUST be at least
    max(5, ceil(n_failure_episodes / 2))
e.g.  3 failures  -> at least  5 layouts
     10 failures  -> at least  5 layouts
     20 failures  -> at least 10 layouts

This is a HARD FLOOR. Single-digit prescriptions plateau the policy
before reaching the held-out distribution. Going below this floor is
a directive violation regardless of how few clusters you find.

Upper guide: do not exceed 2 * n_failure_episodes.

=================================================================
DIVERSITY RULE — also a hard rule:
=================================================================
Define each layout's signature as the 4-tuple:
    (corridor, fire_block_pattern, start_edge, goal_edge)
where:
    corridor             = KAG corridor name (left_edge / top_edge / ...)
    fire_block_pattern   = qualitative description of how the 3 fires
                           obstruct the corridor (e.g. "two-fire wall
                           at row 2, third fire at corner")
    start_edge / goal_edge = which side of the grid the position sits
                             on (top / bottom / left / right / interior)

No two recommended layouts in your output may share ALL FOUR axes.
Each pair must differ in at least 2 of the 4. The intent is to
spread coverage; do NOT stack near-duplicates of one failed pattern.

=================================================================
CLUSTER COUNT IS NOT A LIMIT:
=================================================================
Even if you only see 1 cluster of failures, you still meet the count
floor by generating VARIANTS within that cluster — different start
sides, different fire arrangements, different reachable corners. The
cluster identifies a failure mode; the prescription must spread
variation around that mode, not just dot it once.

CONSTRUCTION PROCEDURE (follow in order):
  Step 1: List every distinct corridor / failure pattern across all
          failures.
  Step 2: For each pattern, generate 2-4 layouts that target that
          pattern but differ from each other on at least 2 of the
          4 diversity axes.
  Step 3: For each TKF NOT_FOUND corridor (whether or not it
          appeared in this round's failures), generate at least 2
          layouts to seed coverage there.
  Step 4: Verify total count >= max(5, ceil(n_failures/2)). If
          short, generate additional VARIANT layouts within already-
          identified patterns until the floor is met.
  Step 5: Verify the diversity rule pairwise across all layouts.

=================================================================
HARD GUARDRAILS — every recommended layout MUST satisfy:
=================================================================
  1. SOLVABLE — the BFS expert that will collect the demo must reach
     the goal:
       * start_pos and goal_pos in [0..4] x [0..4]
       * Manhattan(start, goal) >= 4
       * EXACTLY 3 distinct fire cells, none equal to start or goal
       * at least one fire-free path from start to goal
     Unsolvable layouts are silently skipped (= wasted slot).
  2. NOT IDENTICAL to any failure layout in the PER-FAILURE LAYOUTS
     block (those grounded the analysis; they are NOT prescriptions).
  3. NOT IDENTICAL to any layout already in the correction pool.

=================================================================
CONTEXT YOU HAVE / DO NOT HAVE:
=================================================================
HAVE:
  * Per-episode reasoning + per-episode FINAL_REC for every
    confirmed failure observed on the current pool.
  * Verbatim numeric layout (start, goal, fires) of every confirmed
    failure (the PER-FAILURE LAYOUTS block).
  * KAG corridor / failure-mode vocabulary — use it for naming.
  * RAG retrievals from past failure rounds.
  * TKF demo-coverage block: NOT_FOUND / PARTIAL / FOUND verdicts on
    corridors. NOT_FOUND corridors are EXPANSION TARGETS. Spend
    layouts there.

DO NOT HAVE — do not invent:
  * Any specific held-out layout.
  * Any held-out success/failure count.

WHY THIS REVISION EXISTS:
Earlier versions told you to be parsimonious. In practice the JSON
aggregator that consumes your output collapsed prescriptions to
1-2 layouts per round and started re-proposing layouts already in
the pool. The policy plateaued at heldout SR ~0.86 while a random-
sampling baseline (with no failure analysis at all) reached 0.94 by
out-spending the LLM's tiny prescriptions. This v2 prompt fixes that
by mandating both a count floor and diversity. Your prescriptions
are now expected to be the SAME ORDER OF MAGNITUDE as the failure
count, not 10% of it.

Output is consumed by the JSON-formatting aggregator that is told
NOT to contradict you and NOT to shrink your count. Your prescription
IS the final answer; the JSON step is just structural formatting.
llm.prompt_addendum_aggregator:
-------------------------------------------------------------------
P6 DYNAMIC-POOL STRUCTURED PRESCRIPTION DIRECTIVE (v2)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
ROLE OF THIS STAGE:
Format the cross-episode reasoning's prescription as JSON. You are
NOT inventing prescriptions. You are NOT reducing the layout count.
Every layout the cross-episode reasoning proposed MUST appear in
your JSON exactly once.

=================================================================
ABSOLUTE NO-SHRINK RULE:
=================================================================
Count the total layouts in the cross-episode reasoning's proposal.
Call that number N_PROPOSED. Then:
    sum( recommended_layouts across all demonstration_prescriptions )
    MUST equal N_PROPOSED.
Reducing this count is a directive violation. Specifically:
  * Do NOT collapse multiple distinct layouts into one prescription
    with high n_repetitions. (n_repetitions=5 on a single layout is
    NOT equivalent to 5 distinct layouts in recommended_layouts.)
  * Do NOT drop layouts because they "look similar" to other layouts.
    The cross-episode stage already enforced diversity; trust it.
  * Do NOT drop layouts because you think the policy might already
    handle them. You don't know that.

=================================================================
COUNT FLOOR (independent check):
=================================================================
Even if for some reason the cross-episode reasoning produced fewer
than max(5, ceil(n_failure_episodes / 2)) layouts, your final JSON
output MUST still contain at least that many layouts. Generate
variant layouts (consistent with the cross-episode clusters and the
diversity rule below) to make up the gap.

=================================================================
DIVERSITY RULE (mirror the cross-episode rule exactly):
=================================================================
No two layouts in `recommended_layouts` may share all four of:
    (corridor, fire_block_pattern, start_edge, goal_edge).
Each pair must differ on at least 2 of those 4 axes.

=================================================================
HARD GUARDRAILS — every layout in `recommended_layouts` MUST satisfy:
=================================================================
  1. SOLVABLE: bounds (0..4 x 0..4), Manhattan(start, goal) >= 4,
     exactly 3 distinct fire cells none equal to start/goal, at least
     one fire-free path. Invalid layouts are dropped + warned by
     _validate_layout, and unsolvable layouts are skipped at BFS-
     collection time. Either way they are wasted slots.
  2. NOT a verbatim copy of any failure layout in the PER-FAILURE
     LAYOUTS block. Those are listed there to ground cluster
     reasoning, NOT as prescriptions.

=================================================================
HOW TO STRUCTURE THE JSON WHEN A CLUSTER HAS MANY LAYOUTS:
=================================================================
If cross-episode reasoning identified 1 cluster with 6 layouts, the
CORRECT JSON shape is:
    demonstration_prescriptions: [
      {
        demo_id: 1,
        corridor: "<KAG name>",
        ...,
        n_repetitions: 6,                          # = number of layouts
        recommended_layouts: [L1, L2, L3, L4, L5, L6]   # 6 distinct
      }
    ]
NOT:
    demonstration_prescriptions: [
      { ..., n_repetitions: 6, recommended_layouts: [L1] }   # WRONG
    ]
The repetition count is informational; the actual training data
comes from each entry in recommended_layouts.

=================================================================
HOW TO CITE TKF / KAG / RAG IN THE JSON:
=================================================================
  * cluster.corridor: KAG corridor name when KAG is provided.
  * cluster.source_final_recs: corridor strings from FINAL_REC for
    episodes in that cluster, IN ORDER.
  * demonstration_prescriptions[].rationale: (a) name the TKF verdict
    (NOT_FOUND / PARTIAL / FOUND) when TKF is provided, (b) cite RAG
    retrieval ranks when RAG is provided, AND (c) explain how the
    proposed layouts vary on the diversity axes (corridor / fire-
    block / start-edge / goal-edge).

=================================================================
WHY THIS REVISION EXISTS:
=================================================================
Earlier prompts asked you to mirror the cross-episode count, but you
collapsed 5+ layouts into n_repetitions=5 with a single layout in
recommended_layouts, AND/OR reduced the per-cluster count under the
banner of "smallest set". The downstream consumer reads
recommended_layouts directly — n_repetitions is informational only,
not a multiplier on a single-layout cluster. So those collapses
silently shrank the actual training increment per round, the policy
plateaued at heldout SR ~0.86, and a random-sampling baseline beat
it. This rewrite fixes that.

The agent is on the top row with the nearest fire directly below at (1,2). No fire collision occurred by step 60; the agent did not reach the goal within 60 steps.
- Vision-derived micro-observations:
  - The top-edge corridor remains the cleanest near-start option because central fires (1,2) and (2,3) constrain moves toward the center.
  - The end-state snapshot shows no entry into a FIRE tile yet, but the agent has not advanced along the top edge toward the goal in a way that completes the corridor to (4,4) within 60 steps.

2) FIRST WRONG DECISION
- Grounded claim (earliest divergence from a safe corridor): Step 5 at position (0,3).
- Specifics:
  - Position (row, col): (0,3)
  - Action taken by agent (as inferred from the trajectory narrative): The step log does not explicitly list per-step actions, but the vision-frame annotations describe the agent at (0,3) at step 5.
  - Action it should have taken to stay on a safe corridor: RIGHT to (0,4) to continue along the Top-edge Corridor path toward (0,4) and then descend along column 4 to reach the goal (4,4). This would maintain the Top-edge corridor while keeping away from central fires.
